passages.s: But he whose Book shall be given him behind his back2 Shall invoke destruction: But in the fire shall he burn, For that he lived joyously among his kindred, Without a thought that he should return to God.
Is it that he hath the knowledge and vision of the secret things?
We have not created the Heavens and the Earth and whatever is between them in sport: We have not created them but for a serious end:7 but the greater part of them understand it not.

Be not then one of the despairing." "And who," said he, "despaireth of the mercy of his Lord, but they who err?" He said, "What is your business then, O ye Sent Ones?" They said, "We are sent unto a people who are sinners, Except the family of Lot, whom verily we will rescue all, Except his wife.
No power have they to succour them: yet are their votaries an army at their service.
And remember Noah when aforetime he cried to us and we heard him, and delivered him and his family from the great calamity; And we helped him against the people who treated our signs as impostures.
But I will send to them with a gift, and await what my envoys bring back." And when the messenger came to Solomon, he said, "Aid ye me with riches?
When we are gracious to man, he withdraweth and turneth him aside: but when evil toucheth him, he is a man of long prayers.
And of his signs are, that He sheweth you the lightning, a source of awe and hope; and that He sendeth down rain from the heaven and giveth life by it to the earth when dead.
Make thou therefore the hearts of men to yearn toward them, and supply them with fruits that they may be thankful.
These shall be two signs from thy Lord to Pharaoh and his nobles; for they are a perverse people." He said, "O my Lord!
Is it not enough for them that we have sent down to thee the Book to be recited to them?
Verily in this are signs for those who hearken.
Remember how he hath made you the successors of the people of Noah, and increased you in tallness of stature.
And He is God in the Heavens and on the Earth!
These passages may allude to the ladder set up in a tower by Wacih ben Salamah, one of the ancient doorkeepers of the Caaba, by which he professed to mount up to God and receive divine Oracles.

We appointed the kebla which thou formerly hadst, only that we might know him who followeth the apostle, from him who turneth on his heels: The change is a difficulty, but not to those whom God hath guided.
And if ye be on a journey and shall find no notary, let pledges be taken: but if one of you trust the other, let him who is trusted, restore what he is trusted with, and fear God his Lord.
Surely this present life is only a play, and pastime!
But vile is that for which they have sold it.
And whoever shall obey God and the Apostle, these shall be with those of the Prophets, and of the Sincere, and of the Martyrs, and of the Just, to whom God hath been gracious.
Had we sent down this Koran on some mountain, thou wouldst certainly have seen it humbling itself6 and cleaving asunder for the fear of God.
Three persons speak not privately together, but He is their fourth; nor five, but He is their sixth; nor fewer nor more, but wherever they be He is with them.
And fear ye God: for God is Ready to turn, Merciful.
